title: Harbor and Ledger
premise: In 1848, apprentice clockmaker Mara Kavanagh is summoned to the cliffside observatory to repair its failing master clock, where she discovers a stranger bearing letters in the unmistakable hand of her brother Tomas — declared dead at sea three years ago. The letters reveal Tomas faked his drowning to escape a smuggling ring that now blackmails their father, a harbormaster whose ledgers hide the family's complicity. As evacuation orders fall on the plague-stricken harbor district, Mara must decide whether to expose the truth and destroy her father, or protect the lie and abandon her brother. In the end she forges a third path: she testifies to the smuggling but alters the ledgers to shield the innocent dockworkers, secures the last berth for her father, and leaves on the same boat as Tomas — choosing neither loyalty nor truth, but a new identity built from both.
about_author: Zephyrine Brightwater is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing harbormasters' ledgers along the Atlantic coast, where she first encountered records deliberately altered to hide whole families from history. She writes historical fiction about the people time tried to erase, and lives in a converted lighthouse keeper's cottage with too many clocks.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Gears
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. In her cramped workshop, Mara measures her life in portable things — tools, her mother's ring, a single photograph — as plague rumors stir the harbor. Summoned to the observatory, she climbs the cliff path as the master clock dies. The beat is quiet dread: a world about to come apart, measured in what can be carried.

chapters.title: Letters from a Drowned Man
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Repairing the observatory clock, she finds hidden correspondence in its case — letters in Tomas's unmistakable hand, dated months after his burial at sea. A stranger named Corwin appears, claiming to be the courier. The beat is vertigo: grief overturned, the dead writing to the living, and Mara unable to tell anyone why she's shaking.

chapters.title: Her Father's Neat Hand
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, with a flashback in her father Declan's voice. Searching the harbormaster's office for proof the letters are real, she finds ledger entries in Declan's handwriting matching the letters' dates — payments, silences, complicity. The beat is betrayal: the father she worshipped as an honest man has been buying his son's ghost.

chapters.title: Corwin's Bargain
chapters.summary: Corwin's POV. The courier reveals the smuggling ring's terms: continued silence in exchange for Tomas's safety, and a warning that the quarantine will close the harbor within weeks. He offers Mara a place on the last ship if she delivers a final payment. The beat is temptation dressed as mercy — survival offered at the price of complicity.

chapters.title: What the Clock Remembers
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Restoring the master clock gear by gear, Mara realizes its chimes were altered years ago to mask the smugglers' signals — her own craft implicated. She confronts the observatory's aging keeper, who confesses and gives her a hidden logbook. The beat is reckoning with inheritance: even her beloved trade carries the family's rot.

chapters.title: The Berth List
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The quarantine order arrives; one evacuation berth remains for the Kavanagh family, and Mara holds the paper. Declan assumes it's his; Mara knows Tomas is alive and hiding in the salt caves. The beat is the novel's central wound sharpened: love made arithmetic, one name to be written and one erased.

chapters.title: Salt Caves, Living Brother
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. She finds Tomas alive, hollowed by guilt, who explains he faked his death to shield the family from the ring's retaliation and never expected his father to pay. He begs her to give the berth to Declan. The beat is grief with teeth: reunion poisoned by the discovery that everyone chose lies to protect everyone else.

chapters.title: The Night the Chimes Lied
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Mara and Declan. The ring moves to seize the harbor's remaining ships; Corwin betrays them, and the smugglers come for the ledgers. Declan, cornered, burns the office rather than let his family hang, and Mara watches the man she loved choose destruction over truth. The beat is climax — loyalty and truth tearing the family open at last.

chapters.title: Ink and Ash
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. In the burning office's ruins, Mara salvages the true ledgers and, using her father's own ink and hand, alters them to shield the dockworkers while preserving the evidence against the ring. She names the smugglers to the magistrate and writes Tomas's name on the berth. The beat is resolve: truth served, mercy forged by hand.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. At dawn, Declan surrenders to the magistrate and refuses the berth; Mara gives it to Tomas and boards with him as the observatory clock, repaired, chimes the true hour across the water. The beat is bittersweet release: neither loyalty nor truth wins whole, but Mara carries both — and a new name — into whatever comes next.
